title: SPREAD: Sampling-based Pareto front Refinement via Efficient Adaptive Diffusion
claim: A transformer block injects conditioning into noise prediction through cross-attention, with residual additions and explicit tensor shapes at each stage.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right data flow, repeated block box, shape annotations on every module
description: A single wide architecture diagram that reads left to right. On the left, Noisy Points X_t (n,d) in a purple box feeds an Input Projection. Below it, Timestep t and Condition C sit in a green rounded group. Each is passed through its own Embed layer, and the two embeddings are concatenated into an (n,2,e) tensor. A gray 'DiT Block (×L)' container holds three stages: Layer Norm then multi-head self-attention, Layer Norm then multi-head cross-attention, and Layer Norm then a pointwise feedforward. Thick colored arrows carry the residual stream through circled-plus addition nodes, going from light blue to dark teal. The brown arrow from the concatenation node enters the cross-attention module. The stream then goes to Output Projection and the Noise prediction (n,d) in a pink box. A legend at the bottom explains layers, forward pass, concatenation and element-wise addition. Tensor shapes in italics label every module.
caption: DiT-MOO architecture. Diffusion Transformer adapted for multi-objective optimization, where noise prediction is conditioned on objective values condition via multi-head cross-attention.
abstract: Developing efficient multi-objective optimization methods to compute the Pareto set of optimal compromises between conflicting objectives remains a key challenge, especially for large-scale and expensive problems. To bridge this gap, we introduce SPREAD, a generative framework based on Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs). SPREAD first learns a conditional diffusion process over points sampled from the decision space and then, at each reverse diffusion step, refines candidates via a sampling scheme that uses an adaptive multiple gradient descent-inspired update for fast convergence alongside a Gaussian RBF-based repulsion term for diversity. Empirical results on multi-objective optimization benchmarks, including offline and Bayesian surrogate-based settings, show that SPREAD matches or exceeds leading baselines in efficiency, scalability, and Pareto front coverage. Code is available at https://github.com/safe-autonomous-systems/moo-spread .
